title: Portable export profile: the closed payload and its import
outcome: Portable export profile: the closed payload and its import
acceptance: Portable export uses migration JSON row encoding under a distinct strict portable profile. A source registry classifies every durable table/column, canonical kind, nested variant and reference role; tests compare it with actual schema and durable variants, and unknown names or nested fields refuse without disclosure. Ordinary migration still exports/imports every promised row.

A representative released source with shared and private memory, mediated turns, planning, named roots, verification reuse, environment evidence, failing/superseding evaluations, obligations, native child/root seals and inherited graph history round-trips through staged import and both ordinary full check and portable closure check. Original ids/canonical bytes and dense feed order survive, native completion remains by seal, inherited history stays inherited.

Every private memory version, assertion and head and all live authority, session/connection/grant, delivery/focus/advertisement, retry/result and host-path-policy rows are absent; compare every included/excluded table family. Historical session/grant attribution confers no authority. Receiving-clock live claim or executable offer refuses without rewriting it.

Each executable link and retained feed target resolves to its original included record. Removing any required evidence, policy, producer, root history or feed target produces a named refusal. Excluded feed targets refuse rather than creating placeholders, changing links or dropping dense positions.

Provenance-only exclusions use separately minted stub and field-specific resolution records with the referring canonical bytes unchanged, only for explicitly registered historical readers. A profile with no admitted paths refuses those links. Tests reject unused/mismatched mappings and prove executable lookup never uses them; unknown reader roles refuse.

Mixed-project or unclassified state is refused before host interruption/disclosure and rechecked at the frozen cut. A non-work-item second-project fixture is detected. Payload size/part/traversal bounds refuse instead of truncate, and split payloads reassemble and import. Failure of representative ordinary-history eligibility remains a blocker, not a refusal-only completion.
disposal_reason: Portable handoff was replaced before any of it shipped: docs/features/git-task-sync.md says the previous portable writer-epoch and release/acquire design is gone, AGENTS.md says the selected sync uses no global writer lock, writer epochs or release/acquire protocol, and master has no portable code or brief. Cancelled under Greg's word, 43498a6e #683. Nothing here was built or tested.
